messages.subject: dynamic tabset panels
parts:
Is there a way to dynamically populate a tabset panel with variable number of tab panels? The idea is that depending on the data set being loaded or selected in the Shiny App, variable number of tabs would be created, one per dataset being loaded/selected. I've been trying different strategies using renderUI() and tabsetPanel()/tabPanel() one less successful then the others...

Thanks a bunch.

messages.subject: Re: dynamic tabset panels
parts:
Ok, I figured out a way to produce dynamic tabset panels, it's a bit ugly and would like to have your comments on wether i am denaturing Shiny or not. The simplest way I found was to use a series of call() to build the functions to render the tabset using an lapply() dependent on the reactive value input$samples. The list of calls returned is then evaluated by a do.call() with the function tablsetPanel()

It goes like this

output$plotUI <- renderUI({
    ## Dynamically render tabset based on the user selected samples               
    do.call(tabsetPanel,
            ## Create a set of tabPanel functions dependent on input$samples
            lapply(input$samples,function(s){
                ## Populate the tabPanel with a dataTableOutput layout, with ID specific to the sample.
                ## Can also accommodate additional layout parts by adding additional call() to call("tabPanel")
                call("tabPanel",s,call('dataTableOutput',paste0("table_",s)))
            })
            )
})

Then, the panels can be populated with data using a simple loop structure like this 


lapply(input$samples, function(s){
    ## Add a DataTable of gene selected in the heatmap
    output[[paste0('table_',s)]] <- renderDataTable(values[[s]],options=list(iDisplayLength=10))
    return(s)
})

Obviously, one needs a bit of extra logic to make sure that there is at least one selected samples, etc... Also this structure can be made more complex by adding extra call() arguments to the call("tabPanel") to add additional UI feature to the different tabs (like text, download button, etc...)

I have an almost finished example with quite complex logics on gitub: heatmap-app

Let me know what you think, whether this is an ugly hack or not. I could see that the do.call()/call() structure could be made as a dynamic function taking variable arguments that would hide the ugliness of the structure... 

thanks

Marco
